title: pCloud Pass cyberattack, Nov 2026

subject.name: pCloud Pass
subject.about: pCloud Pass is the password manager made by pCloud, a cloud storage company founded in 2013 that says it has over 24 million users. People use it to keep their passwords and fill them in on any device.

images.title: The pCloud Pass home page
images.alt: The top of the pCloud Pass website, headed "Your Trustworthy European Password Manager", saying pCloud Pass helps you keep your passwords and gives you secure access to them on all your devices.
images.caption: Screenshot of pCloud’s pCloud Pass home page, Nov 28, 2026. pCloud has published no notice about the attack on its own site.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by pCloud, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: One company's password manager and the people who use it. pCloud says only a small number of users' email addresses were exposed and has not given a number.
who_is_affected: People who use pCloud Pass. pCloud says a small number of users' email addresses were exposed and those users were sent a notification. It says stored passwords were not compromised. pCloud says it never asks for your Master Password or recovery words by email, phone or chat.

known.text: pCloud says a cyberattack targeted its pCloud Pass password manager and was promptly contained.
pCloud says a small number of users' email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made.
Customers reported emails saying a new device had connected to their pCloud Pass account.
pCloud has not said how the attackers got in, when, or whether any login attempt succeeded.

not_known.text: Whether any encrypted password vaults were reached or copied.
How the attackers got in, and when.
